spots.name: St Mark's Basilica
spots.summary: The Patriarchal Cathedral Basilica of Saint Mark, commonly known as St Mark's Basilica, is the cathedral church of the Patriarchate of Venice; it became the episcopal seat of the Patriarch of Venice in 1807, replacing the earlier cathedral of San Pietro di Castello.

spots.name: Doge's Palace
spots.summary: The Doge's Palace is a palace built in Venetian Gothic style, and one of the main landmarks of the city of Venice in northern Italy. The palace included government offices, a jail, and the residence of the Doge of Venice, the elected authority of the former Republic of Venice.

spots.name: Piazza San Marco
spots.summary: Piazza San Marco, often known in English as St Mark's Square, is the principal public square of Venice, Italy, where it is generally known just as la Piazza. The Piazzetta is an extension of the Piazza towards San Marco basin in its southeast corner.

spots.name: Bridge of Sighs

hours.note: Closed Wed

spots.summary: The Bridge of Sighs is a bridge in Venice, Italy. It connects the Doge's Palace with the New Prison across Rio di Palazzo.

spots.name: Rialto Bridge
spots.summary: The Rialto Bridge is the oldest of the four bridges spanning the Grand Canal in Venice, Italy. Connecting the sestieri (districts) of San Marco and San Polo, it has been rebuilt several times since its first construction as a pontoon bridge in 1173, and is now a significant tourist attraction in the city.

spots.name: Horses of Saint Mark
spots.summary: The Horses of Saint Mark, also known as the Triumphal Quadriga or the Horses of the Hippodrome of Constantinople, are a group of bronze statues of four horses that originally formed part of a monument depicting a quadriga — a four-horse chariot used in chariot racing and Roman triumphs.

spots.name: St Mark's Campanile
spots.summary: St Mark's Campanile is the bell tower of St Mark's Basilica in Venice, Italy. The campanile is a reconstruction completed in 1912, the previous tower having collapsed in 1902. At 98.6 metres (323 ft) in height, it is the tallest structure in Venice and is colloquially termed "el paròn de casa".

spots.name: Santa Maria della Salute
spots.summary: Santa Maria della Salute, commonly known simply as La Salute, is a Roman Catholic church and minor basilica located at the Punta della Dogana in the Dorsoduro sestiere of the city of Venice, Italy.

photo.author: This Photo was taken by Wolfgang Moroder. Feel free to use my photos, but please

spots.name: Portrait of the Four Tetrarchs
spots.summary: The Portrait of the Four Tetrarchs is a porphyry sculpture group of four Roman emperors dating from around 300 AD. The sculptural group has been fixed to a corner of the façade of St Mark's Basilica in Venice, Italy since the Middle Ages.

spots.name: Gallerie dell'Accademia
spots.summary: The Gallerie dell'Accademia is a museum gallery of pre-19th-century art in Venice, northern Italy. It houses the Leonardo da Vinci drawing The Vitruvian Man, which can only be exposed for a few weeks every six years for conservation reasons.

spots.name: Venetian Lagoon
spots.summary: The Venetian Lagoon, also Venice Lagoon or Lagoon of Venice, is an enclosed bay of the Adriatic Sea, in northern Italy, in which the city of Venice is situated.

spots.name: Venetian Arsenal
spots.summary: The Venetian Arsenal is a complex of former shipyards and armories clustered together in the city of Venice in northern Italy. Owned by the state, the Arsenal was responsible for the bulk of the Venetian Republic's naval power from the Late Middle Ages to the early modern period.

spots.name: St Mark's Clocktower

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Clock Tower in Venice is an early Renaissance building on the north side of the Piazza San Marco, at the entrance to the Merceria. It comprises a tower, which contains the clock, and lower buildings on each side. It adjoins the eastern end of the Procuratie Vecchie.

spots.name: Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari
spots.summary: The Basilica di Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari, commonly abbreviated to the Frari, is a church located in the Campo dei Frari at the heart of the San Polo district of Venice, Italy. It is one of the largest churches in the city and it has the status of a minor basilica. The church is dedicated to the Assumption of Mary.

spots.name: Biblioteca Marciana

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Marciana Library or Library of Saint Mark is a public library in Venice, Italy. It is one of the earliest surviving public libraries and repositories for manuscripts in Italy and holds one of the world's most significant collections of classical texts.

photo.author: This Photo was taken by Wolfgang Moroder. Feel free to use my photos, but please

spots.name: Ca' d'Oro
spots.summary: The Ca' d'Oro, or Palazzo Santa Sofia, is a palace on the Grand Canal in Venice, northern Italy. Ca' d'Oro or Cadoro translates to "House of Gold" or "Golden House" in English because of the gilt and polychrome external decorations that once adorned its walls.

spots.name: Museo Correr
spots.summary: The Museo Correr is a museum in Venice, northern Italy. Located in St. Mark's Square, Venice, it is one of the 11 civic museums run by the Fondazione Musei Civici di Venezia. The museum extends along the southside of the square on the upper floors of the Procuratorie Nuove.

spots.name: Peggy Guggenheim Collection

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: The Peggy Guggenheim Collection is an art museum on the Grand Canal in the Dorsoduro sestiere of Venice, Italy. It is one of the most visited attractions in Venice.

spots.name: Scuola Grande di San Rocco

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Scuola Grande di San Rocco is a building in Venice, northern Italy. It is noted for its collection of paintings by Tintoretto and generally agreed to include some of his finest work.

spots.name: Church of San Giorgio Maggiore
spots.summary: San Giorgio Maggiore is a 16th-century Benedictine church on the island of the same name in Venice, northern Italy, designed by Andrea Palladio, and built between 1566 and 1610.

spots.name: Ponte dell'Accademia
spots.summary: The Ponte dell'Accademia is one of only four bridges to span the Grand Canal in Venice, Italy.

spots.name: Ponte della Costituzione
spots.summary: The Ponte della Costituzione is the fourth bridge over the Grand Canal in Venice, Italy. It was designed by Santiago Calatrava, and was moved into place in 2007, amid protest by politicians and the general public. The bridge was installed in 2008 and opened to the public on the night of September 11, 2008.

spots.name: Santi Giovanni e Paolo
spots.summary: The Basilica dei Santi Giovanni e Paolo, known in Venetian as San Zanipolo, is a Catholic minor basilica and Dominican conventual church in the Castello sestiere of Venice, Italy.

spots.name: Ospedale della Pietà

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ospedale della Pietà was a convent, orphanage, and music school in Venice. Like other Venetian ospedali, the Pietà was first established as a hospice for the needy.

spots.name: Procuratie
spots.summary: The Procuratie are three connected buildings along the perimeter of Saint Mark's Square in Venice, Italy.

spots.name: San Zaccaria
spots.summary: The Church of San Zaccaria is a 15th-century former monastic church in central Venice. It is a large edifice located in the Campo San Zaccaria, just off the waterfront to the southeast of Piazza San Marco and St Mark's Basilica.

spots.name: Hotel Danieli

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Danieli, Venezia, A Four Seasons Hotel is a palatial five-star hotel in Venice, Italy. The central wing of the hotel was built as the Palazzo Dandolo at the end of the 14th century, by one of the Dandolo families. CNN cites it as one of the top five "lavish hotels" in the city.

spots.name: Palazzo Pisani Moretta

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Palazzo Pisani Moretta is a palace situated along the Grand Canal in Venice, Italy, between Palazzo Tiepolo and Palazzo Barbarigo della Terrazza.

spots.name: San Giacomo di Rialto

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: San Giacomo di Rialto is a church in the sestiere of San Polo, Venice, northern Italy. The inclusion of Rialto in the name distinguishes this church from San Giacomo dell'Orio which is situated in the sestiere of Santa Croce, on the same side of the Grand Canal.

spots.name: Ca' Rezzonico

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: Ca' Rezzonico is a palazzo and art museum on the Grand Canal in the Dorsoduro sestiere of Venice, Italy.

spots.name: Palazzo Dario

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo Dario, known as Ca' Dario, is a palace located between the Palazzo Barbaro Wolkoff and the narrow Rio delle Torreselle on the Grand Canal in the sestiere of Dorsoduro, of the city of Venice, Italy. The palace was built in the Venetian Gothic style and was renovated in Renaissance style.

spots.name: Punta della Dogana

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Punta della Dogana is an art museum in one of Venice's old customs buildings, the Dogana da Mar.

spots.name: Palazzo Grassi

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Palazzo Grassi is a building in the Venetian Classical style located on the Grand Canal of Venice (Italy), between the Palazzo Moro Lin and the campo San Samuele.

spots.name: San Giorgio Maggiore
spots.summary: San Giorgio Maggiore is one of the islands of Venice, northern Italy, lying east of the Giudecca and south of the main island group. The island, or more specifically its Palladian church, is an important landmark. It has been much painted, featuring, for example, in a series by Monet.

spots.name: San Pantalon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Chiesa di San Pantaleone Martire, known as San Pantalon in the Venetian language, is a church in the Dorsoduro sestiere of Venice, Italy. It is located on the Campo San Pantalon (square), and is dedicated to Saint Pantaleon.

spots.name: Ponte della Libertà
spots.summary: The Ponte della Libertà is a road bridge connecting the islands that form the historical centre of the city of Venice to the mainland part of the city.

spots.name: La Fenice
spots.summary: Teatro La Fenice is a historic opera house in Venice, Italy. It is one of "the most famous and renowned landmarks in the history of Italian theatre" and in the history of opera as a whole.

spots.name: Ca' Pesaro
spots.summary: Ca' Pesaro is a Baroque marble palace turned art museum, facing the Grand Canal of Venice, Italy. Today it is one of the 11 museums run by the Fondazione Musei Civici di Venezia system.

photo.author: This Photo was taken by Wolfgang Moroder. Feel free to use my photos, but please

spots.name: Ponte degli Scalzi
spots.summary: The Ponte degli Scalzi, is one of only four bridges in Venice to span the Grand Canal.

spots.name: Ca' Foscari

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ca' Foscari, the palace of the Foscari family, is a Gothic building on the waterfront of the Grand Canal in the Dorsoduro sestiere of Venice, Italy.

spots.name: Ca' Vendramin Calergi

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ca' Loredan Vendramin Calergi is a 15th-century Renaissance palace on the Grand Canal in the sestiere (quarter) of Cannaregio in Venice, Italy. It was commissioned by the patrician Loredan dynasty, namely Andrea Loredan, and paid for by Doge Leonardo Loredan.

spots.name: Statue of Bartolomeo Colleoni
spots.summary: The equestrian statue of Bartolomeo Colleoni is a Renaissance sculpture in Campo Santi Giovanni e Paolo, Venice, Italy, created by Andrea del Verrocchio in 1480–1488. Portraying the condottiero Bartolomeo Colleoni, it has a height of 395 cm excluding the pedestal.

spots.name: Palazzo Grimani di Santa Maria Formosa

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Palazzo Grimani of Santa Maria Formosa is a State museum, located in Venice in the Castello district, near Campo Santa Maria Formosa.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Palazzo Grimani di Santa Maria Formosa

spots.name: Scalzi, Venice

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Santa Maria di Nazareth is a Roman Catholic Carmelite church in Venice, northern Italy. It is also called Church of the Scalzi being the seat in the city of the Discalced Carmelites religious order.

photo.author: Tony Hisgett, edited by MenkinAlRire (upright, centered, col.aberration, sharpne

spots.name: Palazzi Barbaro

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzi Barbaro—also known as Palazzo Barbaro, Ca' Barbaro, and Palazzo Barbaro-Curtis—are a pair of adjoining palaces, in the San Marco district of Venice, northern Italy. They were formerly one of the homes of the patrician Barbaro family.

spots.name: Fondaco dei Turchi
spots.summary: The Fondaco dei Turchi is a palazzo in classical Venetian style, later referred to as the Turks' Inn, on the Grand Canal of Venice, northeastern Italy.

spots.name: Palazzo Contarini del Bovolo
spots.summary: The Palazzo Contarini del Bovolo is a small palazzo in Venice, Italy, best known for its external multi-arch spiral staircase known as the Scala Contarini del Bovolo.

spots.name: Last Supper
spots.summary: The Last Supper is a painting by the Italian Renaissance artist Jacopo Tintoretto. An oil painting on canvas executed in 1592–1594, it is housed in the Basilica di San Giorgio Maggiore in Venice, Italy.

spots.name: Scuola Grande di San Marco

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Scuola Grande di San Marco is a building in Venice, Italy, designed by the well-known Venetian architects Pietro Lombardo, Mauro Codussi, and Bartolomeo Bon. It was originally the home to one of the Scuole Grandi of Venice, or seven major confraternities, but is now the city's hospital.

photo.author: This Photo was taken by Wolfgang Moroder. Feel free to use my photos, but please

spots.name: San Salvador

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Santissimo Salvatore, usually known by its Venetian name of San Salvador, is a church in Venice, northern Italy. It is located on the Campo San Salvador, along the Mercerie, the main shopping street of Venice.

spots.name: San Moisè

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Chiesa di San Moisè is a Baroque style, Roman Catholic church in Venice, northern Italy.

spots.name: Santa Maria Formosa
spots.summary: Santa Maria Formosa, formally The Church of the Purification of Mary, is a church in Venice, northern Italy. It was erected in 1492 under the design by Renaissance architect Mauro Codussi.

spots.name: Il Redentore

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Chiesa del Santissimo Redentore, commonly known as Il Redentore, is a 16th-century Roman Catholic church located on Giudecca (island) in the sestiere of Dorsoduro, in the city of Venice, Italy.

spots.name: San Giorgio dei Greci
spots.summary: San Giorgio dei Greci is a church in the sestiere (neighborhood) of Castello, Venice, northern Italy. It was the center of the Scuola dei Greci, the Confraternity of the Greeks in Venice. Around this period there was a similar church in Naples called Santi Pietro e Paolo dei Greci.

spots.name: Santa Maria dei Miracoli, Venice

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Santa Maria dei Miracoli is a church in the sestiere of Cannaregio, in Venice, Italy, designed in 1481 by Renaissance architect Pietro Lombardo and his sons Tullio and Antonio. It was completed in 1489.

spots.name: Piazzale Roma
spots.summary: Piazzale Roma is a square in Venice, Italy, at the entrance of the city, at the end of the Ponte della Libertà, a road bridge. The bridge connects the islands that form the historical centre of the city of Venice to the mainland part of the city.

spots.name: Santa Maria della Pietà

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The church of Santa Maria della Pietà or della Visitazione is a prominent church in the sestiere of Castello in Venice, Italy. It is sited on the Riva degli Schiavoni, a short walk from the Doge's Palace.

spots.name: Ponte della Paglia
spots.summary: Ponte della Paglia is a bridge in Venice, Italy. The current structure dates from 1847, and the original structure was built in 1360. The original structure was the oldest stone bridge in Venice. The name of the bridge is understood to come from boats mooring nearby to offload straw (paglia).

spots.name: Madonna dell'Orto

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Madonna dell'Orto is a church in Venice, Italy, in the sestiere of Cannaregio. This was the home parish of Tintoretto and holds a number of his works as well as his tomb.

spots.name: Mocenigo Palace Museum
spots.summary: A collection of clothes dating from the 18th century. Splendid interior. Collection of dresses and accessories, fabrics, books, figurines in various period costumes. A MUVE museum.

photo.author: This Photo was taken by Wolfgang Moroder. Feel free to use my photos, but please

spots.name: ASAC Library

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: An annex at the Biennale gardens where the Biennale keeps records related to the Biennale exhibitions and to 20th century art, from 1895 onwards.

spots.name: Oratorio dei Crociferi

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Small oratory facing the old monastery dei Crociferi, painting circle by Palma the Younger.

spots.name: Monument for Giovanni Caboto
spots.summary: Venetian explorer of North America who worked for the British (c. 1450-c. 1500).

photo.author: This Photo was taken by Wolfgang Moroder. Feel free to use my photos, but please

spots.name: Palazzo Da Mula
spots.summary: The summer residence of the Venetian patricians. The façade features large Gothic windows and Veneto-Byzantine patere and panels from the 12th and 13th centuries. It is one of the few palazzi which escaped the restructuring of the island in the 1800s.

spots.name: Mekhitarist Monastery

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Library with historical manuscripts, collection of works, miniatures and documents of the Armenian history, Monastery Church. Tours in Italian, English, and Armenian. On the small island of San Lazzaro degli Armeni.
